paper.title_en: Analysis of Boolean functions related to two-party nonlocal games for biased inputs
paper.abstract_en: The CHSH game is the most extensively studied two-party nonlocal game with binary inputs and outputs, while Basak et al. [1 ] recently identified additional games of this type that exhibit quantum advantage under uniform inputs. Motivated by the practical difficulty of generating perfectly unbiased inputs, we investigate these games under symmetric biased input distributions. We determine the optimal classical success probabilities and analyze the corresponding quantum success probabilities within a restrictive family of quantum strategies. Our results show that quantum advantage persists over suitable ranges of input bias even within this restricted quantum strategy family, with both the optimal strategies and the quantum advantage depending on the input bias. Moreover, for all considered games, the quantum advantage is maximized at the uniform input distribution within the considered restricted quantum strategy family.
